Hi Lina — thanks for the note and for sending the accreditation doc. Short answer: yes, BrightLearn looks eligible for our EDU / nonprofit program, subject to verification and a short MSA addendum.

Baseline hosted API (public catalog) rates (typical, USD):
- Text generation: $0.003 / 1k tokens (standard open models)
- Higher-capacity models: $0.012 / 1k tokens (for larger seqs / faster SLOs)
- Embeddings: $0.0008 / vector (standard 1536-d)

Education / Nonprofit program highlights:
- Up to 40% off list for accredited nonprofits (sliding scale based on commit & SLO needs)
- Free trial credits: $2,000 platform credits for evaluation for new EDU accounts
- Option to lock a base monthly commit for deeper discounts and dedicated capacity if needed

Next steps I recommend:
1) I can get you the formal ratecard PDF and a short eligibility checklist (we'll need the accreditation PDF you attached + org EIN / non-profit status).
2) If procurement needs a more formal quote, I'll loop in Sales Ops for a signed pricing sheet and a DocuSign offer for a small monthly commit (if you want the deeper discount).

Attached: redwood-hosted-ratecard-v2.pdf (summary of tiers). I'll also loop Monica from CS to plan an onboarding pilot.

Best,
Karthik

Hey team — quick ops take:
- EDU 40% is available to accredited nonprofits; revenue-generating pilots do not automatically disqualify an org. We evaluate on a case-by-case basis and include a simple MSA addendum to capture allowed use-cases (we ask that student PII be handled per our standard DPA).
- Minimum commit for the 40%: $6,000/month committed (3-month ramp optional). For smaller pilots we can do a 30% "pilot" discount + $2k trial credits (no commit) that converts to the full EDU discount on execution of the commit.
- Data residency / logging: hosted API stores request logs by default for 30 days. For EDU/nonprofit customers with student data we recommend either: 1) a data-retention clause in the DPA reducing retention to 7 days or 2) a Private deployment (VPC) for full control. Both are standard options — Monica can follow up on onboarding implications.

I'll draft a one-page offer sheet:
Option A (pilot): 30% discount, $0 commit, $2k trial credits, standard hosted SLOs.
Option B (commit): 40% discount, $6k/month commit, DocuSign for 3-month term (auto-renews).

If you want, I can prepare the DocuSign link and a pricing sheet by EOD.

—Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
